provenance.instrument: Derry Township Zoning Ordinance of 1997 (Chapter 215 Zoning, adopted 6-18-1997, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 DE2844, Township of Derry, PA. 215-8.1 and 215-10 name Derry Township, Mifflin County, the township website (derrytwp.info, Zoning & Code Enforcement) links its Zoning Ordinance to ecode360.com/9226785, and building permits go to an office in Lewistown, so this is Derry township, Mifflin County, not Derry in Dauphin or Westmoreland. Every district's uses and figures are text in Article II. The four attachments are sign tables. New Laws: none listed. Definitions amended by Ord. No. 2024-1 and 2025-1
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows 'Includes legislation through 12-30-2025'. New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code'
checks: ECHO housing (an elder cottage) is a conditional use in A, R, LDR, MDR and HDR, decided by the Board of Supervisors (215-12C(3), 215-13C(3), 215-14C(2), 215-15C(2), 215-16C(2), 215-11 'Conditional use'). At most two people live in it, at least one related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption and 50 or older, handicapped or disabled (215-69A). The definition says up to two 'elderly, handicapped or disabled persons' who are 'first cousins or closer' to the occupants of the house, and a physician's letter may be required (215-11)

The elder cottage is of portable construction and at most 900 sq ft, with at least 250 sq ft of habitable floor area (215-69B, 215-32C). The lot must meet the district minimum as though the cottage were on its own lot, and the house, existing accessory buildings and the cottage together must stay within the district's lot coverage (215-69C, D). It stands only in a side or rear yard and meets the side and rear setbacks for principal uses (215-69E). Approved water supply and sewage disposal (215-69F). One more off-street space beyond the house's two (215-69G, 215-38B)

The Zoning Officer issues a temporary zoning permit, reviewed every 12 months with a renewal fee. When no qualifying person lives in it, the cottage is removed within three months, turned to another approved accessory use (temporary farmworker housing, a farm or rural occupation), or subdivided or put on a land development plan (215-69H, I). ECHO housing, two-family conversions and temporary farmworker housing are not new principal uses and need no land development plan (215-34)

Two-family conversion: in A, R, LDR, MDR, HDR and VC a detached single-family house that existed on the chapter's effective date (adopted 6-18-1997) and then had at least 2,000 sq ft may be converted into two units by conditional use. No exterior extension or change that would alter its residential character, escape from every floor above grade, approved water and sewage, and 'Four off-street parking spaces shall be provided' (215-108). The parking table gives 'conversion apartment dwellings' one space per '1/2 dwelling unit (i.e., 3 spaces per dwelling unit)' (215-38C(2)(h)), and where the chapter's rules differ 'that regulation which imposes the greater restriction shall apply' (215-5). So the two units need 6 spaces in all. The table cell is itself inconsistent, since one space per half unit is 2 per unit, while it says 3. The apartment needs at least 250 sq ft (215-32C)

Duplexes (two units in one freestanding building, side by side or over and under) are permitted by right in R (on the LDR standards), MDR (5,000 sq ft per unit with public water and sewer) and HDR (3,500 sq ft per unit with both) (215-13B(4), 215-15B(2), E, 215-16B(2), D, 215-11 'Dwelling' (2)). Townhouses are conditional in R and MDR and permitted in HDR, and multiple-family dwellings are permitted in HDR, each three or more units (215-11, 215-106). A planned residential development needs at least 100 acres and a master plan approved by the Board of Supervisors as a zoning map change (215-25A(2)(b)), so it is not a path for one house lot

Temporary farmworker housing: on a farm in A, one mobile home for each 100 acres or fraction of the farm for farmworkers actively engaged on that farm and their families, in a side or rear yard with the single-family setbacks (215-12B(7)(d)). LI, Q and F permit agriculture 'subject to the standards listed in § 215-12' (215-20B(1), 215-22B(1), 215-23B(1)), so whether this accessory housing reaches a farm there is not settled. HC permits as an accessory use 'Housing for students, employees and their families in accordance with the standards of the HDR Zone' (215-19B(9)(d))

Lot coverage in every district is impervious cover, 'buildings, driveways, parking area, sidewalks' (215-11). District accessory yards: A 15 ft side and rear, R 10 ft side and 5 ft rear, LDR 10 ft side and 5 ft rear, MDR and HDR 5 ft side and rear, none in a front yard, and accessory structures at most 15 ft tall (215-12H(4), 215-13G(2), H, 215-14F(1), G, 215-15F(1), G, 215-16E(1), F). The elder cottage instead meets the principal side and rear setbacks (215-69E). ECHO housing is 'An accessory use' (215-11), and an accessory structure is 'A structure associated with an accessory use' (215-11 'Structure'), so the 15 ft accessory height is read as binding the cottage, since 215-69 sets no height of its own

Floodplain Zone, an overlay on every zone (215-24F): 'The following uses and no others are permitted', with additions to existing structures that are not a substantial improvement and 'An accessory structure on the same lot with, and of a nature customarily incidental and subordinate to, the principal structure' added by Ord. No. 2006-2. 'All structures and buildings not specifically permitted' are prohibited, as is any part of an on-lot sewage system (215-24G, I). Whether the elder cottage, an accessory use, comes in as such an accessory structure is not settled. If it does, it still needs public sewer and the 215-24K elevation. On a property adjacent to a perennial stream or water body shown on the Comprehensive Plan Natural Features Map, 215-47C(3)(a) bars any aboveground structure or on-site sewage system 'within the Floodplain Zone nor within 100 feet of the edge of any stream or water body, whichever is greater'. In FE and FA areas no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank (215-24K(7)). In a floodway no work that would raise flood heights, and no new construction without a permit from the DEP Regional Office (215-24K(5)). In FE no new construction unless its effect with all other development raises the 100-year flood by at most one foot (215-24K(6)). A nonconforming structure in a floodway may not be enlarged if the 100-year flood would rise (215-24L(2)). New construction or a substantial improvement of a residence has its lowest floor 1 ft above the 100-year flood with no enclosed space below (215-24K(1), (4)). New construction is a structure begun on or after January 16, 1981, with its later improvements (215-24Q). A special exception or variance in the Floodplain Zone needs all of the listed findings, among them a use that 'Requires a waterfront location' (215-24J(2)), and 215-124D(2)(f) sends variances there to 215-24. A dwelling does not need a waterfront location, so a variance for the cottage there is out of reach in practice. Where no FEMA floodway is mapped, the floodway is assumed to reach 50 ft from the top of the stream banks (215-11 'Floodway')

Natural resources: every zoning permit on land with slopes of 15% or more, woodland, or a stream corridor is reviewed and approved by the Board of Supervisors after the Planning Commission, by the conditional use procedure (215-47A). No structures on slopes over 25%, at least 40% of trees of 5 inch caliper kept or replaced, and a 20 ft wooded buffer along property lines and 100 ft along perennial streams (215-47C). Woodland is land shown as 'conservation' on the Comprehensive Plan Existing Land Use Map, or any other lot with 30% or more tree cover, 'excepting lots of record as of the date of adoption of this chapter' (215-47C(2)). So a lot of record from before 6-18-1997 is woodland only where that map shows it

Agricultural setback: in R, LDR, MDR and HDR no dwelling unit may stand within 50 ft of any land in the Agricultural Zone (215-13G(3) on a separate nonfarm parcel, 215-14F(2), 215-15F(2), 215-16E(2)). In A, on a separate nonfarm parcel, no dwelling may stand within 50 ft of Agricultural Zone land used for agriculture (215-12H(5)). The elder cottage is a dwelling unit, so it keeps this distance

Density: the MDR and HDR tables also give a maximum density that applies to all uses. For a single-family house it is 5 dwelling units per acre in MDR with public water and sewer, 2 with sewer only and 1.5 with water only, and 8 in HDR with both (215-15E, 215-16D). If it were a test on one lot, a house and an elder cottage would need 17,424 sq ft in MDR with both services and 10,890 sq ft in HDR, more than twice the lot minimum. An 8,000 sq ft MDR lot with one house already exceeds 5 units per acre, so the density is read here as a figure for a development, not a test on one lot. That reading is not settled

Nonconforming lots: a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings may be built on a lot of record below the lot minimum that existed on the chapter's effective date, if the yards, height and building area are met, and contiguous nonconforming lots in one ownership merge (215-119). No expansion of a nonconforming structure in any floodplain (215-115A(8))

More than one principal use on a lot must meet every lot and yard rule for each structure as though on its own lot, with land development approval and its own sewage disposal (215-34). No one may live permanently in a tent, travel trailer, bus, boat, camper or motor home (215-33)

A use 'neither specifically permitted nor denied' is denied by the Zoning Officer and referred to the Zoning Hearing Board for an interpretation (215-6). Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 215-124D(2), which follow MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance was found. A variance or special exception lapses without a permit and a start of work within six months (215-126)

value.name: Two-family conversion of an existing house (A, R, LDR, MDR, HDR, VC)
value.conditions: A detached single-family house that existed when the chapter took effect in 1997 and then had at least 2,000 sq ft may be converted into two dwelling units. No extension or change to the outside that would alter its residential character, except fire escapes. Every floor above grade has a direct escape to the ground. Approved water supply and sewage disposal. Four off-street parking spaces under 215-108D, and 6 in all under the parking table and 215-5. The apartment has at least 250 sq ft of habitable floor area. No land development plan is needed (215-34)

requires.condition: The house existed on the chapter's effective date. The chapter was adopted on 6-18-1997
The house contained at least 2,000 sq ft on that date. Floor added since does not count

value.note: 215-108D asks four off-street spaces in all. The parking table asks 3 per unit for 'conversion apartment dwellings' (215-38C(2)(h)), and 215-5 applies the greater restriction, so six in all, 4 beyond the house's two. The table cell is itself inconsistent: it reads '1/2 dwelling unit (i.e., 3 spaces per dwelling unit)', and one space per half unit would be 2. In A a conversion does not count against the new dwellings allowed per tract (215-12E(2))

value.name: Duplex (MDR, HDR)
value.conditions: A freestanding building with two dwelling units side by side or over and under. MDR: 5,000 sq ft per unit, 5 units per acre, lot coverage 40%, lot width 40 ft per unit, front 25 ft, side 15 ft, rear 25 ft. HDR: 3,500 sq ft per unit, 8 units per acre, 45%, width 40 ft per unit, front 20 ft, side 10 ft, rear 20 ft. Both only with public water and public sewer. Each unit at least 700 sq ft. Three off-street spaces per unit

requires.condition: Public sewer. The duplex figures are given only for a lot with both public water and public sewer

value.note: 10,000 sq ft in MDR and 7,000 sq ft in HDR are two units at the per-unit figure. Whether adding a unit beside or above an existing house makes a duplex, rather than a two-family conversion (which needs a conditional use and allows no outside extension), is not settled. The parking table's duplex cell reads '1/2 dwelling unit (i.e., 3 spaces per dwelling unit)', which is itself inconsistent, and 215-5 applies the greater figure, 3 per unit

value.name: Duplex (R)
value.conditions: A freestanding building with two dwelling units side by side or over and under, 'subject to the standards of § 215-14' (the LDR table: 10,000 sq ft with public water and public or alternative sewer, 20,000 sq ft with sewer only, 32,000 sq ft with water only, one acre with neither). Each unit at least 700 sq ft. Three off-street spaces per unit

The parking table's duplex cell reads '1/2 dwelling unit (i.e., 3 spaces per dwelling unit)', which is itself inconsistent, and 215-5 applies the greater figure, 3 per unit

value.name: Temporary farmworker housing (A)
value.conditions: On a farm, one mobile home for each 100 acres or fraction of the farm, for farmworkers actively engaged in farm work on that farm and their families. In a side or rear yard, meeting the single-family setbacks. Approved water supply and sewage disposal. Occupied at least three months a year by someone working on the farm, or removed within three months. Not subdivided off the farm unless counted in the tract's dwelling quota. At least 250 sq ft of habitable floor area

requires.condition: The property is a farm of at least 10 acres used for gain in agriculture
The occupants are farmworkers actively engaged in farm work on that farm, and their families

disputed_districts.note: LI, Q and F permit agriculture 'subject to the standards listed in § 215-12'. Whether that brings in the farmworker housing that 215-12B(7)(d) allows as an accessory use in A is not settled. The stronger reading keeps it to A

historic_bypass.note: The zoning chapter has no historic path for ECHO housing

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists a dwelling, ECHO housing or a conversion. HC permits housing for students, employees and their families as an accessory use on the HDR standards (215-19B(9)(d))

value.condition: The elder cottage is occupied by no more than two people, at least one of whom is related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption and is 50 or older, or handicapped, or disabled. The definition adds that they are first cousins or closer, and a physician's letter may be required for a disability.

The elder cottage is of portable construction, placed in a side or rear yard, and meets the side and rear setbacks for principal uses. It is removed within three months once no qualifying person lives there, unless turned to another approved accessory use or subdivided. The Zoning Officer issues a temporary zoning permit reviewed every 12 months.
The house, existing accessory buildings and the elder cottage together stay within the district's lot coverage, which counts all impervious surface.
An approved system of water supply and sewage disposal serves the elder cottage.

Agricultural setback: in R, LDR, MDR and HDR no dwelling unit may stand within 50 ft of any land in the Agricultural Zone (in R, on a separate nonfarm parcel). In A, on a separate nonfarm parcel, no dwelling may stand within 50 ft of Agricultural Zone land used for agriculture. The elder cottage is a dwelling unit.

Floodplain Zone: only the listed uses are permitted, all structures and buildings not specifically permitted are prohibited, and no part of an on-lot sewage system may be placed there. In FE and FA areas no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank. On a property adjacent to a perennial stream or water body on the Comprehensive Plan Natural Features Map, no aboveground structure may stand in the Floodplain Zone (215-47C(3)(a)). Ord. No. 2006-2 added an accessory structure to the uses the Floodplain Zone permits (215-24G(5)), but the chapter applies the greater restriction where its rules differ (215-5). A variance in the Floodplain Zone needs all of the 215-24J(2) findings, among them a use that requires a waterfront location, which a dwelling does not.

disputed_by.note: Ord. No. 2006-2 permits 'An accessory structure on the same lot with, and of a nature customarily incidental and subordinate to, the principal structure' in the Floodplain Zone, and the elder cottage is an accessory use (215-11, 215-34). Under that reading the cottage may stand there, with public sewer (no on-lot system in the Floodplain Zone, 215-24I(4)) and the 215-24K elevation, except on a property adjacent to a mapped perennial stream (215-47C(3)(a))

no_variance.note: Every special exception or variance in the Floodplain Zone needs all of the 215-24J(2) findings, and a dwelling does not require a waterfront location. 215-124D(2)(f) sends variances there to 215-24

value.condition: Stream corridors: on a property adjacent to a perennial stream or water body shown on the Comprehensive Plan Natural Features Map, no aboveground structure and no on-site sewage system within 100 ft of the edge of the stream or water body.

Floodplain Zone, for work on the house: additions to existing structures that are not a substantial improvement are permitted, no nonconforming structure may be expanded in any floodplain, and new construction or a substantial improvement of a residence has its lowest floor 1 ft above the 100-year flood with no enclosed space below. In a floodway no work that would raise flood heights, no new construction without a DEP permit, and no enlarging a nonconforming structure if the 100-year flood would rise. In FE no new construction unless all development together raises the 100-year flood by at most one foot. New construction is a structure begun on or after January 16, 1981, with its later improvements. A variance there needs a use that requires a waterfront location.

Natural resources: a zoning permit on land with slopes of 15% or more, woodland, or a perennial stream corridor is reviewed and approved by the Board of Supervisors by the conditional use procedure. No structures on slopes over 25%. Woodland is land shown as conservation on the Existing Land Use Map, or another lot with 30% or more tree cover, except lots of record when the chapter was adopted on 6-18-1997.
